title: RouteBenchScenario
description: One RouteBench scenario. DEFINITION ONLY — nothing in this directory executes a benchmark. Design ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §8.2 §11·§12·§44·§45 splits RouteBench in two: scenario/fixture/baseline DEFINITIONS are tracked here next to the lane-1 eval JSONL, while run RESULTS and reports stay local under `_benchmarks/routing/` because `_benchmarks/` is gitignored (.gitignore:15). Vocabulary is transcribed from MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 11 (baselines B0..B6), section 12 (13 task classes, 17 metrics) and section 45 (scoring keeps raw metrics, no composite). Draft-07 is deliberate: the repo resolves ajv 6.12.6 transitively, which cannot compile 2020-12 — same reason as execution-profile.schema.json.

id.description: Stable slug. Used as the completed-pair key so a re-run can skip finished work (MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md:715 'benchmark가 재실행 가능하고 completed pair를 skip하는 패턴').

title.description: Human-readable one line. Not an identifier.

task_class.description: MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 12 verbatim, all 13 values. The doc calls this list a MINIMUM ('최소'), so widening is expected — but widening must edit this enum, which is the point: an unlisted class is schema-invalid rather than silently benchmarked.

baselines.description: Which baselines this scenario must be compared against. MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 11 makes B0..B4 mandatory ('반드시 비교') and B5..B6 optional ('선택'); this schema does not encode that split because a single scenario may legitimately run a subset. B2 is the Shadow control group per design ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §8.2 §11·§12·§44·§45.

items.$comment: B0 Fixed Sonnet · B1 Fixed Opus · B2 Current v4 Policy · B3 v5 Static Heuristic · B4 v5 Adaptive Router · B5 Fixed Fable · B6 Hindsight Oracle (offline hindsight policy).

metrics.description: Metrics this scenario reports. MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 12 lists 17; section 45 forbids compressing them into a single composite score up front and requires raw metrics to always be preserved, so there is deliberately no `score` property on this schema.

replay_mode.description: MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 13 / section 46. Exact = a recorded outcome exists for the candidate; partial = only some candidates have real outcomes; simulation = learned or predicted outcome. The doc requires this distinction to stay visible rather than being averaged away, because a replay is not a full counterfactual.

fixture.description: Where this scenario's input material lives. A scenario may be defined before its fixture exists — `status: "pending"` is how that is declared instead of shipping an empty fixture file that a runner would silently treat as zero cases.

status.description: `pending` means the fixture is owned by other work and does not exist yet. A runner MUST refuse to score a pending scenario rather than scoring it as empty.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the fixture, when it exists. Omitted while status is pending and the owning task has not landed a path yet.

owner.description: Which task or lane owns producing this fixture. Present so a pending entry names someone rather than rotting anonymously.

why.description: What routing behaviour this scenario is meant to discriminate. Same discipline as the nl-activation cases: an expectation with no stated reason cannot be re-judged later.

source.description: Which design clause this scenario comes from. Required for the same reason `source` is required in nl-activation.cases.jsonl — without it nobody can tell later whether a changed expectation is a fix or a regression.
